title: Dedicatory Inscriptions
subtitle: Ten votive offerings to the gods — LVGVS, ROSMERTA, BELENVS, TARANIS, ESVS.
objectives: Read ten complete votive inscriptions from southern Gaul.
Recognize the dative singular endings -ui, -vo, -i for divine names.
Translate the formula DEDEMIT IEVRV ("gave, dedicated to the sacred place").
Understand the religious function of votive epigraphy.

sections.heading: Votive inscriptions and the gods
sections.body:
A votive inscription records a gift to a deity. The dedicator sets up a stone, an altar, or a statue and inscribes it with the formula:

X DEDEMIT Y-dat. IEVRV

"X gave (this) to Y, to the sacred place."

The god's name appears in the dative case. The formula IEVRV ("to the sacred place") marks the dedication as ritual. Votive epigraphy was the primary way Gauls interacted with their gods in writing.

sections.heading: The major gods
sections.body:
The Gaulish pantheon, as preserved in inscriptions, includes:

LVGVS (Lugus) — god of all skills, identified with Mercury
ROSMERTA — goddess of abundance, often paired with Mercury
BELENVS (Belenos) — god of light and healing, identified with Apollo
TARANIS — thunder god, identified with Jupiter
ESVS — god of sacrifice, associated with trees
EPONA — horse goddess, popular in cavalry units
SEQVANA — goddess of the Seine river
BELISAMA — "most bright", a goddess of light

These names recur in hundreds of dedications across Gaul, Britain, and the Rhineland.

sections.heading: Inscription 1: To Lugus
sections.body:
From Autun, 1st century CE:

SEGOMĀROS VILONEOS DEDEMIT LVGVO IEVRV

Parsing:
SEGOMĀROS VILONEOS — "Segomaros son of Viloneos"
DEDEMIT — "gave"
LVGVO — dative singular, "to Lugus" (the ending -vo is a dative variant for -o- stem nouns)
IEVRV — "to the sacred place"

Translation: "Segomaros son of Viloneos gave (this) to Lugus, to the sacred place."

sections.heading: Inscription 2: To Rosmerta
sections.body:
From Alise-Sainte-Reine, 1st century CE:

PRISCA ROSMERTAE AVVOT

Parsing:
PRISCA — "Prisca" (a Latin name)
ROSMERTAE — dative singular, "to Rosmerta" (the ending -ae is a Latinized dative for -ā- stem nouns)
AVVOT — "vowed"

Translation: "Prisca vowed (this) to Rosmerta."

sections.heading: Inscription 3: To Belenos
sections.body:
From Vaison-la-Romaine (Greek script), 1st century BCE:

ΣΕΓΟΜΑΡΟΣ ΟΥΙΛΛΟΝΕΟΣ ΒΗΛΗΝΟΙ IEVRV

Transliteration:
SEGOMAROS OUILLONEOS BĒLĒNOI IEVRV

Parsing:
SEGOMAROS OUILLONEOS — "Segomaros son of Ouillo"
BĒLĒNOI — dative singular, "to Belenos" (Greek ending -οι represents Gaulish dative)
IEVRV — "to the sacred place"

Translation: "Segomaros son of Ouillo (dedicated this) to Belenos, to the sacred place."

sections.heading: Inscription 4: To Taranis
sections.body:
From Saint-Marcel, 1st century CE:

ATEPOMĀROS TARANIS DEDEMIT

Parsing:
ATEPOMĀROS — "Atepomaros"
TARANIS — dative singular(?), "to Taranis" (the ending -is may be a nominative used as dative, or a scribal error)
DEDEMIT — "gave"

Translation: "Atepomaros gave (this) to Taranis."

sections.heading: Inscription 5: To Esus
sections.body:
From Autun, 1st century CE:

DAGOMĀROS ESVI IEVRV

Parsing:
DAGOMĀROS — "Dagomaros"
ESVI — dative singular, "to Esus" (the ending -vi is a dative variant)
IEVRV — "to the sacred place"

Translation: "Dagomaros (dedicated this) to Esus, to the sacred place."

sections.heading: Inscriptions 6-10: Short dedications
sections.body:
Six more votive inscriptions, from various sites in Gaul, 1st century BCE to 1st century CE:

6. SEQVANAE AVVOT — "Vowed to Sequana"
7. EPONAE DEDEMIT — "Gave (this) to Epona"
8. BELISAMAE IEVRV — "To Belisama, to the sacred place"
9. LVGVO MAPONOS — "To Lugus Maponos" (compound deity)
10. ROSMERTAE LVGVO — "To Rosmerta and Lugus" (paired deities)

These short dedications are the most common type of Gaulish inscription. Learn the structure and you can read hundreds of them.

items.prompt: What is the formula for a votive dedication?
items.answer: X DEDEMIT Y-dat. IEVRV ("X gave (this) to Y, to the sacred place").

items.prompt: What case are divine names in when they receive dedications?
items.answer: Dative, with endings -ui, -vo, -vi, or -i depending on the noun stem.
"Segomaros gave (this) to Lugus, to the sacred place."
"Vowed" — a votive formula, related to Latin vovit.

items.prompt: Which god was identified with Roman Mercury?
Which goddess was paired with Mercury/Lugus?
Which god was identified with Roman Jupiter?

items.answer: "To Belisama" (dative, "most bright", a goddess of light).

sections.heading: Divine names in the dative
sections.instructions: These are the gods of Gaul as they appear in votive inscriptions. Memorize them.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 2.10 covers the Gaulish verb: what we know and what we do not. Third singular -IT, third plural -ONT, preterite -S, and the verb DEDEMIT as the backbone of the corpus.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark complete when you can translate all ten votive inscriptions, recognize the dative forms of divine names, and recite the formula DEDEMIT IEVRV.
